 MISSOULA, Mont. — The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has announced two recalls involving Bose speaker batteries and Vanderhall electric off-road vehicles due to fire and crash hazards.
 Bose speaker battery recall 
 Bose is recalling approximately 634,759 lithium-ion battery packs used in its S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ portable Bluetooth speakers because the batteries can overheat and catch fire.
 The company has received seven reports of batteries melting, smoking or catching fire, including six reports of property damage. No injuries have been reported.
 The affected batteries were sold with speakers and separately as replacement parts or accessories from December 2017 through July 2026. Individual batteries cost between $100 and $160, while speaker systems sold for approximately $700.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled batteries and contact Bose for a free replacement. The speakers can still be used with AC power after the batteries are removed.
 Recalled batteries should not be placed in household trash or regular recycling bins.
 Vanderhall off-road vehicle recall 
 Vanderhall North America, based in Provo, Utah, is recalling approximately 190 model-year 2024 through 2026 Brawley GTS electric recreational off-road vehicles because of defective seat belts.
 The seat belts can lock in the fully retracted position, preventing drivers and passengers from buckling up and increasing the risk of injury in a crash.
 The company has received 11 reports of seat belts locking up. No injuries have been reported.
 The vehicles were sold through Vanderhall dealerships in several states, including Montana and Utah, from April 2024 through June 2026 for approximately $50,000.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled vehicles and contact an authorized Vanderhall dealer to schedule a free repair. Dealers will install inserts in the seat belt guides to prevent the belts from locking.
